hypothesis: Weather foundation models such as Aurora, Pangu-Weather, and GraphCast—trained on large-scale reanalysis datasets like ERA5 and leveraging transformer-based architectures—can produce high-resolution, accurate global weather forecasts that rival or surpass traditional numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems; these capabilities can be directly leveraged for renewable energy planning by improving solar irradiance and wind forecasts, enabling more efficient scheduling and dispatch of variable renewable generators, and reducing the cost of intermittency in power systems. Specifically, the multi-domain generalization of foundation models (covering weather, air quality, and wave forecasting) provides planners with richer, more reliable meteorological inputs across multiple timescales, while ML-driven optimization of unit commitment and real-time pricing can further integrate these forecasts into grid operations. Together, advances in weather foundation models and ML-based power system scheduling represent a synergistic pathway toward higher renewable penetration and lower greenhouse gas emissions.
